title: Runtime F: Codex CLI through the Airline Connector
lede: Codex reaches the same Airline Connector as Meta's Muse (runtime B). What differs: who adds it, how it gets a client ID, which PingOne app signs Sam in, and who calls /mcp. Not tried yet. Loopback callbacks are already allowed, so this is the shortest to try.

steps.title: Ready to use
steps.what: The company has already added the connector: Company ships .codex/config.toml: [mcp_servers.airline] url = {{origin}}/mcp; or pushes it through MDM; requirements.toml allowlist.
steps.why: The CLI has no directory, so the company ships the config instead.

steps.title: Ask
steps.what: Sam asks Codex: "How many airline points do I have?".

steps.title: Call, no token
steps.what: Codex picks loyalty_balance from the Airline Connector and calls /mcp. It has no token yet.
steps.why: The model chooses from the tool names and descriptions. The airline's name in them is what steers it.

steps.title: 401, sign in
steps.what: /mcp answers 401 with metadata: sign in at /connector/authorize, PKCE S256, scope mcp.
steps.why: Codex learns where to sign in from the server, not from config.

steps.title: Authorize
steps.what: Codex codex mcp login airline: registers itself, then sends Sam to /connector/authorize. Muse starts the PingOne sign-in with Muse's connector app, because Codex has no app of its own.
steps.why: Fix the port with mcp_oauth_callback_port so the callback is predictable.

steps.title: Protect check
steps.what: PingOne runs the DaVinci flow: password, Protect risk, MFA on medium risk. Protect sees the connector app and flags an agent; it cannot tell which one.
steps.why: The agent is recognised by PingOne, not by its own word. The screen must say how it knows.

steps.title: Consent
steps.what: PingOne shows the "AI agent detected" screen, then asks Sam to let Codex act for him. Sam agrees.
steps.why: No consent, no token: a "no" ends the flow with nothing issued.

steps.title: Exchanges, token
steps.what: Muse does the code swap and both exchanges with Muse's connector app, then gives Codex its own access token at /connector/token.
steps.why: The PingOne token never leaves Muse. Codex holds only a Muse token for scope mcp.

steps.title: Call with token
steps.what: Sam's own machine calls /mcp with that token. Muse calls the gateway, which checks the delegated token, and the points come back.
steps.why: Not tried yet. Loopback callbacks are already allowed, so this is the shortest to try.
